newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Europe rains too little to solve problem.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Europe rains too little to solve problem.

text.p: Weekend rain has boosted plant growth in the farms and gardens of western Europe, but it was not enough to solve the water supply problems created by the longest spell of dry weather for more than 200 years, according to forecasters and water industry experts.

In contrast to Canada's Manitoba province, where residents were evacuated over the weekend in the face of the Red River floods, British and French experts warned that the rain had done nothing to raise water levels in rivers and reservoirs.
"It did the crops some good, but it wasn't enough to replenish water tables," one French forecaster said.

England also still faces a long term problem. "It's just not sufficient rain to resolve a long term problem, an East Anglian based spokeswoman for the Environment Agency, which controls the abstraction of water by farmers for irrigation, told Reuters.
"The rain wasn't enough to replenish ground water supplies," after a two year spell of dry weather, she said.
The rain has boosted crops. "It's done a power of good," a farmer in the UK's important producing region of East Anglia said.
East Anglian farmers reported damage to crops from the dry period, while France's largest farm union, the FNSEA, warned that irreversible harm had been done to winter grains.
Forecasters expected the dry weather to return from Wednesday after a few more showers.
"The weather is set to turn dry again on Wednesday and this could last until Saturday," a Meteo France forecaster said.
And a spokesman for the UK's Meteorological Office predicted high pressure, bringing dry weather with it, from Wednesday until Friday, the outer limit of normal forecasting.
Between Friday and Sunday, 18 millimetres of rain fell on south-eastern England, the London Weather Centre said. Most of Northern Ireland, England and Wales had rain, a spokesman said.
Meteo France said an estimated 10 mm fell across France over the weekend, bringing parched crops some relief after a three-month dry spell.
A further 3-5 mm was forecast for eastern France on Monday, and scattered showers were also expected in the southwest.
In the Beauce grain belt, weekend rain was heavier than expected, reaching 20 mm.
Western Europe looks dry again for much of this coming week, independent forecaster Weather Services Corp said on Monday.
WSC's latest three-to-five day forecast said the British Isles would be dry from Wednesday to Friday, with mild temperatures.
Elsewhere in western Europe, any showers lingering in the east early in the period would end and the weather would turn dry and seasonable in the east of the region, and warmer to the west.
Germany and central Europe would see a chance of showers, with cool conditions in the east but dry and seasonable weather in the west.
Mediterranean Europe would be wet and cool from Italy through to Greece, but generally dry and milder in western areas from Wednesday to Friday, WSC said.
